title: ALP shared board preset
description: Schema for a shared board definition under metadata/boards/<name>.yaml.  Referenced from project board.yaml files via the top-level `preset:` field.  Exists only as SDK-internal plumbing so multiple projects targeting the same physical board (e.g. the EVK + its ~40 demo apps) share one source of truth for chip population + E1M-pad routing.  Customers building a custom board put these fields inline at the top level of their board.yaml instead.

name.description: Board name.  Used in include/alp/boards/alp_<name>_routes.h + as the board identity in generated Doxygen blocks.

hosts_som_families.description: SoM families this board mechanically + electrically supports (alif-ensemble, renesas-rzv2n, ...).  The validators reject `board.yaml` files that pair a shared board preset with a SoM preset whose `family:` is not listed here.

populated.description: Per-component populated flags.  Keys match chip-driver / block names; each `true` enables the corresponding CONFIG_ALP_SDK_{CHIP,BLOCK}_<name>=y.

e1m_routes.description: E1M-pad routing.  scripts/gen_board_header.py reads this block and emits include/alp/boards/alp_<name>_routes.h.

i2c_devices.description: On-board I2C device instances (chip address / strap facts, optionally with power-monitor calibration).  scripts/gen_board_header.py reads this block and emits `#define <macro> 0x..u` (+ per-entry `alias` + `calibration` shunt/max-current macros) into include/alp/boards/alp_<name>_routes.h.  Single source of truth for chip-instance addresses that used to be hand-authored in the board header.

overlay_pins.description: Board-repurposed pads exposed past the standard E1M pinout's 52 entries, for boards that expose them to an `alp,pin-array` devicetree overlay (see zephyr/dts/bindings/alp,pin-array.yaml).  Each entry gets `EVK_PIN_OVERLAY_BASE + N`, where N is the entry's position in THIS list (0-based) -- an ordinal, not an independent hardware fact, so it is never written by hand; scripts/gen_board_header.py computes it from list order via `enumerate()`.  Reordering entries changes every macro after the moved one, exactly like reordering the backing devicetree overlay's `gpios` phandle list would.

defaults.description: Reference-design app defaults (e.g. canonical display chip, primary IMU).

audio.description: Carrier audio path (codecs + I2S bus + MCLK + I2S path-mux + amp control GPIOs) the Linux DT / audio-graph-card is generated from.  Captures device-instance facts (I2C addresses, L/R channel, mux + shutdown/IRQ GPIO macros) beyond the E1M-pad routing in e1m_routes.

hw_revisions.description: Per-rev metadata (min/max SDK versions, board_id ADC channel + thresholds, status, notes).

additionalProperties.description: Same `status:` shape as $defs/hw_rev_entry in hw-revisions-v1.schema.json (kept in lockstep by hand -- this file's validator loads standalone, with no cross-file $ref resolution).  additionalProperties stays true here (not false, unlike the family-level schema) because board presets carry extra per-rev keys the family schema doesn't (board_id, notes).

route_entry.description: Mirrors board.schema.json's route_entry (the shared preset carries the same e1m_routes shape a customer would write inline).  Keep the two in lockstep.

doc.description: One-line Doxygen @brief documenting what the pad is wired to on this board.

active_low.description: Board convention -- pressed/asserted = 0 V.  Documentation only; the app passes ALP_GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW at alp_gpio_open() time if it wants auto-inversion.

pull.description: Physical pull-resistor present on the PCB (board-static fact).  Apps still pass the matching ALP_GPIO_PULL_{UP,DOWN} at alp_gpio_open() time -- this field documents what the board ships with, it does not drive the controller's internal pulls.

debounce_ms.description: RC-debounce time constant in milliseconds for the board's hardware debounce (mostly buttons).  Documentation hint; the app may add software debounce on top.

board_alias.description: Portable cross-EVK alias (e1m-spec STANDARD.md §7.2 common role). gen_board_header.py emits `#define <board_alias> <macro>` into the generated routes header. The SAME board_alias MUST be declared on every board that exposes the role (enforced by tests/scripts/test_board_alias_parity.py).

route_entry_list_gpio.description: GPIO routes.  Accepts the IO pads (E1M_GPIO_IO<N>) and the GPIO-secondary index of any analog/timer pad (E1M_GPIO_PWM<N> / ADC<N> / DAC<N> / ENC<N>_<X|Y>).  The `E1M_X_` prefix form covers the 45x65 E1M-X form factor's connector namespace.

i2c_device_entry.description: One on-board I2C device instance: schematic strap-selected address (+ optional current-monitor calibration).

macro.description: C macro name emitted as `#define <macro> <address>u`.  `EVK_` for the 35x35 E1M carrier, `XEVK_` for the 45x65 E1M-X carrier (same two-namespace convention as `E1M(_X)?_...` pad names).

part.description: Chip-driver key (bmi323, icm42670, bmp581, tcal9538, tca6408a, tas2563, ina236, ...) -- not a vendor MPN.

alias.description: Extra macro name emitted as `#define <alias> <macro>` (e.g. a shorter convenience name for a device populated in only one variant).

doc.description: One-line Doxygen @brief documenting the strap / collision / respin context.

broadcast_address.description: True when `address` is a broadcast / global-call address multiple devices on this bus legitimately answer BY DESIGN (e.g. the TAS2563 family's 0x48 global-call write-only address, metadata/chips/tas2563.yaml). Excludes this entry from scripts/validate_metadata.py's duplicate-(bus,address) collision check (#1845). Do NOT set this to silence a real strap conflict between two unrelated devices -- document a real conflict via `doc:` instead and fix the strap.

calibration.description: INA236-style current-monitor calibration for this instance.

shunt_ohms.description: Shunt resistance in ohms, as a decimal string (preserves the exact digits emitted into the `f`-suffixed C float literal).

max_current_a.description: Rail max current in amps, as a decimal string (see `shunt_ohms`).

assembled.description: Population status of this instance on THIS board revision: true (default, fitted) or false (DNI on this revision). Mirrors the `assembled` key on SoM presets, and exists for the same reason: without it the default `true` silently asserts that a part is present, and a consumer will emit a devicetree node for silicon that is not on the board. Keep the entry with `assembled: false` rather than deleting it -- the footprint is real and other revisions populate it.  LIMITATION as of 2026-09-05: scripts/gen_board_header.py does NOT read this key -- it emits the address macro for every entry, fitted or not. So `assembled: false` is documentation today, not suppression. Firmware that must not touch an unfitted part has to check this metadata, because the macro's existence proves nothing about the board.

overlay_pin_entry.description: One board-repurposed pad exposed past the standard E1M pinout, addressed by `alp,pin-array` position rather than an E1M pad token.  No `e1m:` / index field -- the index is this entry's position in the containing `overlay_pins:` list, computed by the generator.

macro.description: C macro name emitted as `#define <macro> (EVK_PIN_OVERLAY_BASE + N)`, N = list position.  `EVK_` only -- `_emit_overlay_pins()` hard-codes `EVK_PIN_OVERLAY_BASE ALP_E1M_GPIO_COUNT` (the 35x35 count) with no E1M-X branch, so an `XEVK_PIN_*` entry would emit a base macro from the wrong pinout's GPIO count. Widen this in lockstep with the generator if the 45x65 carrier ever needs its own overlay_pins:.

doc.description: Doxygen @brief: which standard E1M pad was repurposed (E1M name + Alif pin) and what it now does on this board.
